title: Wren and the Current
premise: Wren Amberdale, a disgraced railroad engineer, inherits her missing brother Jonah's compass and a map of closed mountain lines — and the debt he owed men who now want it paid in full. When a government survey team vanishes above the treeline, leaving gear intact and no tracks in the snow, the search party realizes the vanished surveyors found something on the glacier that someone powerful wants buried. Wren must lead a small crew over the range ahead of the snows, racing the brief calving window that opens — and closes — the high route. In the end she reaches the ice cave where the survey team sheltered, uncovers her brother's fate, and must choose between exposing the truth and destroying the map to save the one person she loves from the men who sent them.
about_author: Ines Winterbourne is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent six seasons mapping high alpine passes before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people small against enormous landscapes, from a cabin she refuses to disclose the location of.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Borrowed Compass
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren receives notice of her brother Jonah's debts and a parcel containing his compass and map of closed lines. The men who hold the paper give her thirty days. Emotional beat: grief curdling into obligation — she never wanted the inheritance, but she can't let his name die owing.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. A government survey team fails to report in. Wren, hired for her knowledge of the closed lines, joins the recovery party and finds their camp intact — food, instruments, coats — and not a single footprint leaving it. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread; the mountain is keeping something.

chapters.title: The Debt Collectors Ride the Same Train
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Wren and Elias Voss, the survey financier's fixer. Voss boards their supply train, polite and lethal, asking after the map. Wren realizes the vanished team was sent to find what Jonah was mapping — and that her brother's debt and the disappearance are the same debt. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. The glaciologist on the crew, Suri Okonkwo, explains the calving window: three days when the ice bridge opens a passable route, then seals it for the winter. They must move now or not at all. Emotional beat: commitment — Wren burns her return ticket and takes point.

chapters.title: What the Closed Lines Were Closed For
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, with a flashback chapter from Jonah's field journal. Following the dead map, they find the old tunnel the railroad sealed decades ago — and evidence the closure hid a collapse that killed workers, covered up by the same family that now employs Voss. Emotional beat: the inheritance is a wound, not a gift.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: POV: Suri. A storm splits the party. Two men are lost, and Wren anchors a rope line for six hours to keep the rest alive, costing them a full day of the window. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal — every hour of safety is paid for in margin.

chapters.title: The Man Who Came Back Down
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. They find one surveyor alive, half-frozen, who refuses to say what happened to the others and begs them to turn around. That night he disappears from camp, leaving Jonah's field notebook. Emotional beat: love against duty — Wren realizes Jonah went back up for someone, and she understands the pull completely.

chapters.title: Voss at the Ice Bridge
chapters.summary: POV: Elias Voss. Voss and his men intercept them at the calving route, having used the same window. He offers Wren her brother's debt forgiven in exchange for the map and silence. Emotional beat: the temptation of a clean exit, and the recognition that Voss intends no witnesses either way.

chapters.title: The Ice Gives Way
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. The calving begins early. In the chaos Wren leads Voss's men onto the failing bridge, uses the glacier itself as the judge she can't afford to be, and reaches the ice cave where Jonah and the last surveyor sheltered — and where Jonah's final entries name the men who sent him to die. Emotional beat: climax; fury and clarity in equal measure.

chapters.title: A Map With One Line Open
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Descending ahead of the sealing snows with the evidence, Wren faces the choice: publish and be hunted, or burn it and live. She sends copies to three newspapers and keeps the compass. Emotional beat: resolution — the inheritance she finally accepts is not the debt but the route, and she walks it open-eyed.
